abstract: Parse ProForma 2.1 peptide sequences and calculate masses, fragments, and isotopic distributions in Python.

metadata.description: Parse ProForma 2.1 peptide sequences and calculate masses, fragments, and isotopic distributions in Python.
metadata.name: peptacular

releases.body:
### Fixed

- Every digest function now drops the parent's charge and its labile and unlocalised modifications from each product instead of copying them onto every peptide, which gave every product the wrong mass. A digestion product is a different molecule from the sequence it was cut out of: it does not carry the parent's charge, and neither a labile nor an unlocalised modification names the residue it sits on, so neither can be asserted of any one product. `pt.digest("PEPTIDEKTIDER/2", "trypsin")` returned `PEPTIDEK/2` and `TIDER/2`, each 2.014553 Da heavy by the parent's two protons, and `pt.digest("{Glycan:Hex}PEPTIDEKTIDER", "trypsin")` put the one Hex on both products, counting 162.0528 Da twice. Isotope labels and static modification rules are still copied, because a global label applies to every residue and a static rule applies to whichever products carry the residue it targets. This covers `digest`, `simple_digest`, `semi_digest`, `left_semi_digest`, `right_semi_digest` and `nonspecific_digest`. `ProFormaAnnotation.slice` is unchanged: slicing an annotation is not digesting it. That makes one previously true equality false, which is a visible change in what `digest` returns: for a parent carrying a charge, a labile modification or an unlocalised modification, a digest product is no longer the same string as the matching `annot[span].serialize()`, and it differs by exactly those three things. A test in this repository asserted that equality, so anyone who built on it was building on the wrong product masses this entry fixes.
- `estimate_isotopic_distribution` is importable from `peptacular.sequence`, which is where `docs/migration.rst` says the sequence-based estimate lives. It was listed in `peptacular.sequence.isotope.__all__` but left out of the package namespace, so only `ProFormaAnnotation.estimate_isotopic_distribution` or the submodule path reached it. The migration guide also read as though `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution(annotations=...)` became `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution(sequence=...)`. It never did: `pt.estimate_isotopic_distribution` takes a neutral mass in 4.x and 5.0 alike, and that row now names the paths that exist.

### Changed

- Optional-dependency floors are now the lowest release that actually passes the tests exercising them on Python 3.12, measured version by version instead of inherited. `mcp>=2.1.1,<2.4` becomes `mcp>=2.0.0,<3`: 2.0.0 is the first release with `mcp.server.MCPServer` (1.30.0 raises `ImportError`), and the old `<2.4` capped a version that has never been published. `pydantic>=2.13,<3` becomes `pydantic>=2.12,<3`, which is mcp's own minimum rather than ours. `alphabase>=1.9` becomes `alphabase>=1.0.3`: all 19 published releases below 1.0.3 install on Python 3.12 and all 19 fail the same terminal-modification round trip, leaving `Acetyl@Any_N-term` and `Amidated@Any_C-term` unregistered, and 1.0.3 is the first that passes. `psm-utils>=1.0` becomes `psm-utils>=0.9`: our surface is two API points and works back to 0.2.3, but 0.9 is the last pre-1.0 line and the oldest range we would actually fix. `numpy>=1.26` is unchanged and minimal, forced by cp312 wheel availability.
- `pyteomics>=5.0` is tightened to `pyteomics>=5.0.1`. Nothing was broken: pyteomics declares no unconditional dependencies at any version, and 5.0 declares exactly the same dependencies as 5.0.1, so 5.0 only reaches the interop path when `lxml` and `numpy` are already installed, which `peptacular[pyteomics]` does not provide. One resolution effect is worth naming: in the `interop` extra this floor resolves `psm-utils` 1.5.4 rather than 1.5.5, because `psm-utils` 1.5.5 caps `pyteomics<5` — by its own changelog a precaution against the next major release rather than a measured break. Nothing conflicts or fails, so the resolver takes the older `psm-utils` silently.
- The `alphabase` and `interop` extras now declare `pandas>=2.1.2`. The alphabase converters already imported pandas at run time without declaring it. 2.1.2 is the floor rather than 2.1.1, the first release with a cp312 wheel, because 2.1.1 requires `numpy>=1.26.0` with no upper bound: numpy 2.x then loads against a wheel built for the numpy 1.x C ABI and importing pandas raises `numpy.dtype size changed`. 2.1.2 added `numpy<2`, which sits inside our own `numpy>=1.26`. 2.2.2 is the first release to support the numpy 2 ABI.
releases.name: v5.1.0
